title: Generate Parentheses
description: Generate all well-formed parentheses combinations for n pairs, pruning invalid branches early by tracking open and close bracket counts.

blocks.text: Given n pairs of parentheses, generate all combinations of well-formed (validly balanced) parentheses strings of length 2n.

blocks.caption: Tracking open and close counts directly lets only valid partial strings ever be built, avoiding wasted exploration.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Field","Details"],"rows":[["Input","n (number of parenthesis pairs)"],["Output","All well-formed parentheses strings of length 2n"],["Well-formed","Every prefix has at least as many '(' as ')', and the total counts are equal"]]}

blocks.text: Generating all strings satisfying a structural validity constraint is a backtracking problem, but the key optimization is PRUNING: instead of generating every possible string of opening and closing brackets and checking validity afterward, track the counts of each bracket used so far and only make a move that COULD lead to a valid string, never exploring branches that are already doomed.

blocks.title: Connection
blocks.text: Tracking open and close counts (rather than validating after the fact) is a form of constraint propagation during backtracking, pruning invalid branches as early as possible instead of generating and filtering.

Picture building a string one character at a time, keeping a running balance of open brackets used and close brackets used. An open bracket can always be added as long as fewer than n have been used so far. A close bracket can only be added if fewer close brackets have been used than open brackets, otherwise the string would become invalid immediately (more closes than opens at some point).

blocks.caption: A close bracket is only valid while fewer closes than opens have been used so far.

items: Track two counts: open (opening brackets used) and close (closing brackets used).
Add ')' whenever close < open, since that guarantees the string never goes "negative" (more closes than opens at any prefix).

blocks.content: {"headers":["Step","Choice made","String so far","open, close"],"rows":[["1","add '(' (open 0 < 1)","(","1, 0"],["2","add ')' (close 0 < open 1)","()","1, 1"],["3","length 2 = 2n, record","()","complete"]]}

blocks.title: Answer
blocks.text: For n=1, the only valid combination is "()", matching the expected output exactly.

A direct approach generates ALL 2^(2n) possible strings of '(' and ')' (choosing each character freely) and filters out the invalid ones afterward using a balance-check pass. This is correct but wastes enormous effort generating and then discarding invalid strings.

Tracking open and close counts directly during generation prunes invalid branches the INSTANT they would become invalid, so the recursion only ever explores paths that could still lead to a valid final string, never wasting time on doomed branches.
Generate every possible string of '(' and ')' of length 2n by trying both characters at every position, then filter to keep only the valid (balanced) ones.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Metric","Value","Why"],"rows":[["Time","O(2^(2n) * n)","Every one of the 2^(2n) strings is generated, each validated in O(n)"],["Space","O(2^(2n) * n)","Every generated string, valid or not, briefly exists during generation"]]}

blocks.title: Bottleneck
blocks.text: The vast majority of generated strings are invalid and immediately discarded; pruning during generation avoids this waste entirely.

Track open and close counts throughout the recursion. Only add '(' if open < n, and only add ')' if close < open. This guarantees every string built along the way is a valid PREFIX of a well-formed string, and every complete string of length 2n produced this way is automatically fully valid.

items: Base case: once the current string reaches length 2n, it is guaranteed valid, so record it directly.
Try '(' whenever open < n, recursing with open+1.
Try ')' whenever close < open, recursing with close+1.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Approach","Time","Space"],"rows":[["Brute Force, generate all then filter","O(2^(2n) * n)","O(2^(2n) * n)"],["Optimized, prune with open/close counts","O(4^n / sqrt(n))","O(4^n / sqrt(n))"]]}

blocks.title: Note
blocks.text: O(4^n / sqrt(n)) is the exact count of valid combinations (the nth Catalan number), so the optimized approach does no wasted work beyond generating the valid outputs themselves.

items: Tracking a validity-relevant count (here, open and close brackets used) directly in the recursion prunes invalid branches immediately, instead of generating everything and filtering afterward.
A backtracking solution that only ever builds valid partial results does no wasted work beyond the actual valid output count.
This "track just enough state to prune early" technique is a general upgrade path from a naive generate-and-filter backtracking solution.

blocks.text: Generate Parentheses is solved by tracking open and close bracket counts during backtracking, adding an opening bracket whenever the budget allows and a closing bracket only when it would not exceed the opens used so far. This prunes every invalid branch immediately, generating exactly the valid combinations with no wasted exploration.
